scores.visual_critic_note: UI chrome is clean and controls are thoughtfully organized with a good Tableau10 palette, but the 900×900 circle pack cuts off at the bottom of the visible viewport and the dark edge bundles are visually muddy against the colored circles they traverse.
scores.encoding_integrity_note: scaleSqrt used correctly for force-layout node sizing, key functions present on both node and link data joins, domains derived from data via d3.extent/root.height — radial sqrt transform on the sunburst mildly distorts ring-area-per-depth but is a common accepted practice, not a lie-factor violation.
scores.stress_test_note: The easing parameter sliders trigger a full layout recalculation and 1500ms flubber morph transition on every pixel of movement with no debounce, creating a severe Update Storm that queues cascading transitions.
scores.cognitive_load_note: 300 edges across 200 nodes collapse into a near-hairball at the center in the default circle-pack view, and the control panel (8 layout modes, tension slider, 3 checkboxes, easing selector, FPS display) front-loads enough complexity that a viewer must mentally parse the tool before extracting any insight — hover-to-highlight rescues individual connections but can't be assessed from a static screenshot.
flags: Update Storm - easing param sliders fire updateLayout() (full 1500ms flubber morph for all nodes) on every input tick with no debounce (line 744)
Update Storm - tension slider fires redrawLinks() re-rendering 300 link paths on every input event with no debounce or RAF coalescing (line 747)

Mid-Flight Race - force layout starts a detached nodeSelection path transition (line 589) outside the main transition pattern; switching layouts mid-morph does not guarantee interruption of this orphaned transition
Mouse-Touch Fight - drag and node interactions use no touch event filtering, event.preventDefault(), or sourceEvent checks

proposer:
818 lines, down 14 from 832. The changes:
- Inlined `hierarchyLine` generator — a `d3.line()` for exactly 2 points replaced with a direct `M...L...` path string (more efficient, fewer lines)
- Simplified initial position setup using idiomatic D3 `.each()` + `.attr()` chain instead of `d3.select(this)` inside each
- Removed 4 unnecessary `delete` statements for temporary interpolation properties that get overwritten on every `updateLayout` call anyway
